title: Roman law and the civil-law tradition
summary: Roman law began, by tradition, with the Twelve Tables of about 450 BCE. It grew into a large body of statutes, case rulings and jurists' writings, which Justinian's lawyers summed up in the Codex Iustinianus of 528 to 534 CE. Roman law was revived in the Middle Ages and was developed further in the Napoleonic Code. Today the civil-law tradition built on it, with written codes rather than judicial precedent, is the most widely adopted legal system, found across Europe, Latin America, Asia and Africa.
